entries.3346d67d999d87b8: A reportable segment whose main focus areas are electronics, mobility, and medical & healthcare, handling vehicle interior materials, leather, film, urethane, industrial materials, shock-absorbing materials, and others. From the fiscal year ended March 2026, the three previous categories of "Shoes Business," "Plastics Business," and "Industrial Materials Business" were replaced as reportable segments by three categories: "First Business Division," "Second Business Division," and "Shoes BU (Business Unit)." Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥49,910 million (up 7.8% from the previous fiscal year), and segment profit was ¥3,287 million (up 228.0% from the previous fiscal year). In addition to an increase in gross profit due to higher sales of film for the highly profitable medical field and of industrial materials, the cost of sales ratio improved through cost reductions such as consolidated production at manufacturing sites.

ACHILLES USA, INC., in the United States, is a sales company for film products, and its revenue (excluding internal revenue between consolidated companies) exceeds 10% of consolidated revenue. Research and development centers on plastic processing (molding, film formation and foaming), the company’s core technology, and R&D expenses for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥1,060 million. It receives technical assistance from Germany’s A.S.Création Tapeten AG on the design and manufacturing technology and sales of wallpaper, and pays a fixed percentage of revenue as royalties.

entries.7f85a44ed638d4ec: A reportable segment responsible for the shoe business. It releases new products that respond to health-conscious trends and changes in lifestyle under brands such as the comfort shoes "Achilles Sorbo," the running shoes "BROOKS," and "Shunsoku." Net sales for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥8,928 million (down 11.7% from the previous year). They fell below the previous year due to continued weak consumer spending, against a background of a declining birthrate and sluggish department stores, and the effect of price revisions. The segment loss was ¥321 million, an improvement from the loss of ¥972 million in the previous fiscal year, owing to price revisions, a review of procurement costs, and cost reductions.
